findings.statement: The State plan must provide for a review of drug therapy before each prescription is filled or delivered, and applicable state law must establish standards for beneficiary counseling; the State must give pharmacies detailed compliance guidance (counseling, profiling, documentation), which pharmacies pass to their pharmacists [42-CFR-456.705(a)].

The State plan must provide for point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review using predetermined standards before each prescription is filled or delivered, screening for potential drug therapy problems of specified types [42-CFR-456.705(b)].

Screening must cover: (1) therapeutic duplication (two or more drugs from the same therapeutic class where the combined daily dose risks an adverse result or adds cost without added benefit); (2) drug-disease contraindication; (3) adverse drug-drug interaction; (4) incorrect drug dosage (dosage = strength x quantity dispensed / day's supply, outside the predetermined standard) [42-CFR-456.705(b), 42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].

Screening must also cover: (5) incorrect duration of drug treatment (exceeding or falling short of predetermined standards); (6) drug-allergy interactions; and (7) clinical abuse/misuse (situations within the definitions of abuse, gross overuse, overutilization, etc.) [42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].

To support this review, the State agency must require pharmacists to make a reasonable effort to obtain, record and maintain patient profiles including name/address/phone/DOB or age/gender, significant individual history (disease states, known allergies and drug reactions, comprehensive medication and device list), and pharmacist comments [42-CFR-456.705(d)].

Prospective and retrospective DUR are not required for drugs dispensed to residents of nursing facilities that comply with the Part 483 drug regimen review procedures, though a State agency may elect to make such drugs subject [42-CFR-456.703(b)].

arguments.summary: Eastvale's GLP-1 prescribing fell sharply right after the prior authorization requirement took effect July 1, 2024: from a pre-period mean of 12.1 to 9.8 prescriptions per 1,000 member-months, an 18.6% drop (95% CI -20.8% to -16.2%), which is both statistically significant and material. The timing lines up almost exactly with the policy date (the first post quarter fell 21.4% from 12.45 to 9.79), and EV's SGLT2 and insulin prescribing were flat at the same time, which argues against a broad data artifact. That said, this is a pre/post association, not proof the PA requirement caused the drop; other concurrent factors cannot be ruled out.

findings.statement: The authoritative EV GLP-1 prior authorization effective date is 2024-07-01 (EV-MAN-2024-PH); bulletin EV-BUL-2024-007's 2024-06-01 date is superseded by EV-BUL-2024-011, which postponed the start to July 1, 2024.
GLP-1 prescriptions per 1,000 member-months averaged 12.094 pre-policy (2023Q3-2024Q2) vs 9.846 post-policy (2024Q3-2025Q2), a -18.6% change, 95% CI [-20.8, -16.2]; verdict: significant_and_material.

The quarterly trend is flat before the policy (11.8-12.5 from 2023Q1 through 2024Q2) and drops immediately in 2024Q3 (9.79) and stays near 10 or lower through 2025Q2 (9.97) - a 21.4% single-quarter drop at the policy date.
EV SGLT2 (15.16 in 2024Q2 to 15.20 in 2024Q3) and insulin (25.07 to 24.65) prescribing did not fall at the same time, suggesting the GLP-1 decline is not explained by a system-wide reporting change.

The PA criteria themselves limit approval to type 2 diabetes with A1c >= 7.0 after a metformin trial, or BMI >= 35 with a documented weight-related comorbidity, with 12-month approvals - a narrower population than unrestricted access.

arguments.confidence_reason: The effect is large, statistically significant, temporally aligned with the effective date, and absent in two other drug classes in the same state. But it is a single-state observational pre/post comparison with only four pre and four post quarters and no control state, so causal attribution remains limited.
caveats: Pre/post differences are associations, not proof of causation; concurrent policy, benefit-design, or market changes in EV were not examined.
Only final quarters through 2025Q2 were used; 2025Q3 and 2025Q4 are provisional (claims lag) and were excluded, though they show further declines (8.74 and 6.79 rx/1,000 mm).
Suppressed cells (<11 prescriptions) exist: 12 in EV overall, 8 within the analysis window; suppressed values are treated as missing, not zero.
The superseded bulletin EV-BUL-2024-007 named a 2024-06-01 start; using that date would misplace the break, so 2024-07-01 was used.
Data and states are synthetic (NL Northland, EV Eastvale, SP Southport).
